Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Do you
understand and consent to that?
A: Yes, I understand.
Q: Please start by describing where you were when the collision happened.
A: I was driving through League City on a weekday afternoon, heading to a store on the far side of the intersection. I
needed to make a left turn across the traffic lanes.
Q: Can you tell me what the signal was showing when you began your turn?
A: It was a green light for my direction, but the oncoming traffic had a gap, and I started the turn when I thought it was
clear. Then a vehicle came through from the opposite direction and struck the front passenger side of my car.
Q: Did you see that vehicle before you started moving?
A: No, I didn't. It came into view just as I was already partway through the turn. I braked, but there wasn't time to
avoid it.
Q: How fast do you think you were going when you began the turn?
A: I was going slowly, probably about twenty miles per hour, since I was turning.
Q: Were you hurt in the collision?
A: Yes. My right knee hit the dashboard and the pain has been significant. I went to an urgent care clinic that same
day and was told I may have a ligament injury. I've been using a brace and I'm scheduled for an MRI.
Q: Have you been able to work since the accident?
A: I've missed several shifts because standing for long periods is very painful.
Q: Thank you. Is there anytihng else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'd like the other driver's insurance information documented, and I'm happy to send the clinic records.
Q: Understood. Thank you for your time today.
</page>

address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
